$comment: Term base. The vocabulary a translation must not reinvent — derived from the 1,449 Spanish strings that already shipped, so a new pass agrees with the old one instead of introducing a second word for the same thing. Add a row when a term first appears; a reviewer reads this before the catalog.

register.$note: Informal throughout — measured on the existing translations, 166 tú-forms against 27 usted. A fitness app addresses the person training, not a customer. French is the opposite: vous throughout, measured at 118 vous-forms against 62 tu. Do not assume one register carries across languages.

doNotTranslate.$note: Product and brand nouns. Kept in English by the existing translations, so keep them.

es.$regimenNote: Changed from 'Régimen' to 'Programa' on 2026-08-15 (kegan's call). Two reasons. 'Rutina' was translating BOTH Regimen (29 keys) and Routine (8), so the app's two distinct objects were the same word in Spanish; and 'Régimen' reads dietary or clinical to a Spanish speaker — régimen alimenticio — which is wrong for a training program. 'Programa' mirrors what French already does (Programme/Routine) and leaves 'Rutina' to mean Routine only. 47 keys converted, with gender agreement: el programa, este programa, ¡Programa creado!, Nombre del programa.

fr.$note: THE OPEN COLLISION, and the first thing a native reviewer should settle. 'Série' translates BOTH Streak (60 keys) and Set (68 keys) — measured 2026-08-15, so 128 user-facing strings use one word for two unrelated things. 'Série' is the standard French term for a training set and cannot move, so STREAK is the side that needs a different word. Spanish keeps them apart (Racha / Serie) and has no such problem. Deliberately NOT changed by the 2026-08-15 consistency pass: choosing the word for a streak is a feel judgment across badge names, coach prose and notifications, and a machine pass is not what should make it. Candidates a reviewer might weigh: 'Flamme' (the convention French users know from Duolingo and Snapchat — legible but a borrowed metaphor), 'Suite' (neutral and literal, but flat), 'Régularité' (describes what a streak measures, but does not work as a count noun).
